fetcher.py:610 `return snapshot` returns the (possibly empty) dict with no guard for the all-projects-failed case

The single-project path is documented as failing closed specifically to avoid writing 'an empty all-deletions snapshot' (fetcher.py:545-546), but that protection does not extend to the multi-project all-fail case
ABSENCE: the new test only exercises one failing + one succeeding project (test_fetch_multi_project.py:206-208 seeds OK+BAD); no test covers all-mapped-projects-fail
advisory.finding: The new per-project isolation guards the one-fails-others-succeed case, but when EVERY mapped project's base query fails (len(project_list)>1, all raise transport errors), each is skipped/alerted and _build_snapshot returns an empty snapshot, which downstream differs read as a mass all-deletions event — the same catastrophic outcome the single-project path deliberately fails-closed to avoid. This multi-project all-fail path is untested.

Existing SilentTruncationError/BackendPaginationStallError tests target _iter_pages / single-project / transport facades, not the new multi-project per-project isolation loop
advisory.finding: The new single-project fail-CLOSED branch (`if not _isolate_projects: raise`) is not exercised by any test. `test_single_project_fallback_is_regression_identical` uses a healthy `_FakeClient`, so a regression that removed the re-raise (or flipped `_isolate_projects`) would let a single-project transport failure silently produce an empty snapshot — the mass-deletion failure mode this change exists to prevent — with no failing test.
merged_from: The new per-project truncation re-raise (`except (BackendPaginationStallError, SilentTruncationError): raise`) inside the multi-project loop is not covered by any new/changed test. The resilience test injects only an HTTPError; existing truncation tests exercise the `_iter_pages` machinery / single-project path, not the new per-project loop's fail-loud-past-isolation contract. Widening the broad `except Exception` isolation to swallow a truncation signal for a multi-project pass would not be caught.
scenarios: An unseeded store (single _query_project) hits an ACLI transport error and the fetcher must re-raise rather than write an empty all-deletions snapshot
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `test_single_project_base_query_failure_fails_closed`: seed no projects (or one key), use `_PartialFailClient({}, failing_project=<the single key>)`, and assert `with pytest.raises(urllib.error.HTTPError): fetcher.compute_snapshot(...)`.
